unresolved_risks: BLOCKING CONFLICT: tests/test_rb1_recovery_store.py:533 (test_nginx_service_never_mounts_recovery_volume) reads docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.prod.yml by relative path and scans the nginx service block's text for 'recovery', directly enforcing RB.1 contract section 9.11 against those two files' literal content. Deleting either file breaks this test (FileNotFoundError) in an environment where its cryptography dependency is installed (the project's CI/full-regression run). That test module is outside this movement's 'Files you may read' and editable-tests list, and both the brief and AGENTS.md forbid resolving this by editing the test away ('do not weaken or delete any test', 'report it rather than editing it away'; 'Removal only. If removing a file would break a live code path or a passing test, stop and report it'). Per AGENTS.md Authority hierarchy, this is reported as a genuine contradiction between AC-1 (unconditional deletion) and the brief's own stop-and-report clause, not resolved unilaterally.

Because docker-compose.yml/.prod.yml cannot be deleted without a prior decision, deploy/nginx/default.conf was also left in place: deleting it alone would leave docker-compose.yml's own bind-mount pointing at a missing file, a self-inflicted breakage strictly worse than leaving the equipment intact. Same reasoning kept Dockerfile in place (docker-compose.yml's `build: .` would otherwise dangle).
Because the equipment stays, AC-1 and AC-2 are not met this session: docker-compose.yml/.prod.yml still exist and their own header comments still instruct a reader to run `docker compose up`.

Downstream reword targets (.env.example, utils/runtime_config_source.py, .github/workflows/validation.yml comments, deploy/secrets/README.md) were all left unedited: each currently describes equipment that still physically exists in the repository, so rewording them now -- ahead of the equipment's actual removal -- would make the documentation inaccurate rather than correct.
